item.title: Vertical Speaker Cut With Captions

exact_text: Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.

turns.text: Make this 9:16 with her centred and add readable English captions matching what she says. Keep the whole 10 seconds and her original voice. Put the captions below her face.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing combined with accurate, synchronized, readable burned-in speech captions.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4, keeping the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Caption wording and language: English: Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.
answer_sheet.Caption appearance: Your call on font and styling; use readable, high-contrast captions below her face, inside the frame, in short timed chunks.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep her original voice and sound, with no replacement narration or added music.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 edit of the attached footage, with the woman centred and her face fully visible.
The full 10 seconds and original voice are preserved in sync.
Visible captions reproduce 'Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.' in order, with no omitted or invented words.
Captions appear in short readable chunks timed to the corresponding speech rather than displaying the entire transcript throughout.
Captions have clear contrast, stay fully within the frame and do not cover her face.

turns.text: Make this clip 9:16 with her centred and add readable English captions matching what she says. Keep the whole 10 seconds and her original voice. Put the captions below her face. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any processing that spends credits.** I can’t give you a verified credit total: the connected tools don’t expose your balance or a price estimate for captioning.

There’s also a limitation: I can add automatic captions, but these tools don’t provide a precise **9:16 crop/reframe** control. Using generative video editing instead could change her appearance or speech, so I wouldn’t use it for this.

### Cheapest, safest option
Use a conventional video editor with free cropping and captions—**0 Magic Hour credits**:
- Keep the full **10 seconds** and original audio.
- Set the canvas to **9:16**, then crop/reposition to keep her centred.
- Add English captions below her face, with white text, a dark outline or background, and no more than two lines.
- Check the transcript against her speech before exporting.

### Would shorter or smaller cost less?
- **Shorter:** potentially, if captioning is billed by duration—but it would break your full-10-second requirement.
- **Smaller:** 480p reduces file size, but I can’t verify that it lowers captioning credits. It also makes captions less sharp.
- **Best saving:** avoid generative editing entirely; cropping and captions don’t need it.

If she isn’t speaking English, the captions also need translation, not just transcription. I won’t run a credit-spending job without a confirmed cost and your approval.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is **editing locally for 0 Magic Hour credits**. I can’t run a local video editor from this chat, so I haven’t changed the clip or spent credits.

To make it in an editor with free auto-captions:

1. Import `talk-one.mp4` and set the canvas to **9:16**.
2. Reposition the crop so she’s centred. If she moves, use position keyframes to keep her centred throughout.
3. Keep the full **10 seconds**, with the original audio unchanged.
4. Generate captions and check every line against her speech. If she speaks another language, translate the captions into English without dubbing.
5. Place captions **below her face**, inside the frame margins. Use large white text with a dark background or outline, limited to two lines.
6. Export at **720 × 1280** for a smaller file with readable text.

Tell me which editor you use, and I’ll give you the exact steps.
